reviews.title: Nice case but plan your wiring - Read Below
reviews.comment: Overall the case is very nice and arrived in perfect condition. All six of the stock case fans work fine. If you're not going with liquid cooling and plan to add more fans like I did, I would suggest moving the two side intake and the rear exhaust down to the bottom. Leave the other three on the top. The reason for this is that the stock fans are 6pin and connect to an adapter cable that has your 3pin argb and 4pin pwm. There are two adapters cables, each of which connect 3 fans, but each branch that connects to a fan is pretty short, and spreading the fans apart will make it near impossible to connect all of them. As others have mentioned, a full atx board goes right to the bottom of the case. You'll only be able to fit flat cables under the board, and even that is a bit challenging. PLAN YOUR WIRING OUT AHEAD OF TIME AND GET YOUR CABLES IN PLACE BEFORE INSTALLING YOUR MOBO. You'll never fit anything under there once the mobo is in place. The rear chamber was spacious enough for all of the excess cable, granted I didn't install any drives back there. I'm no expert at cable management, but I was able to get everything tucked and tied without having to force the back on lol.  I ended up using the HDD compartment in the top right for a fan hub. This is a very nice looking case and has a spacious interior for airflow. If you plan everything out ahead of time you shouldn't have too much trouble.
reviews.author: Kathy

reviews.title: Good case, but best for a micro ATX motherboard
reviews.comment: The pros: good looking, solidly built, quiet fans, air flow, dust filters, easy to assemble, price. The cons: build space, cable cutouts, cable management. This is a good case overall, but it’s definitely best for a *MICRO ATX* motherboard. You can use a standard ATX, but space is limited. I think cases need silicon cable cutout liners (to hide where the cords are stored and eliminate sharp edges; aesthetically more pleasing). Also, there are no cutouts and absolutely no space at the bottom, if you’re using an ATX MB (standard/full size MB), to route cables which, if you’re a stickler for cable management/going for the neatest look you can get, you’re better off spending a little extra for a case that has those features. This is my first build, and it wasn’t so bad that I couldn’t finish, but I will likely upgrade cases somewhere down the line for a more user friendly and cleaner looking case. Overall, great case for the price and I believe this might be one of the best (price to performance) if you’re doing a micro ATX build.

reviews.title: Outstanding !!!!!
reviews.comment: I have built lots of PC's and have never had a case which was better for an easy install. Having the power supply behind the motherboard is much better than having it on the bottom. Sure the case is wider but that means plenty of room for cables instead of the customary squeeze job with a standard ATX case. I used an ATX motherboard and I don't see why some had problems with it. Asus Aura Sync worked perfeclty for the RGB fans and they are very quiet . I would not hesitate to but this case again. It's an amzing value
